fieldMarks: Short tail and thin straight bill; 20.6-23.1 cm
Black with purple and green gloss in spring and summer
Fresh fall plumage heavily marked with white spots, wearing off through winter
Bill bright yellow in breeding season (base of lower mandible blue in males, pink in females), duller otherwise
Juveniles all dusty gray with dark bills
behavior: Usually forages in flocks, mostly on the ground probing soil; sometimes takes fruit in trees or insects in the air
Mostly insects, berries and seeds; often imitates other birds
Northern birds mostly move south in fall, migrating by day; southern birds may be permanent residents
habitat: Cities, parks, farms, open groves and fields; almost any disturbed habitat, usually scarce in extensive wild forest, scrub or desert.
range: Native to Eurasia; introduced in New York City in 1890. Now breeds from southeastern Alaska across southern Canada and south through most of the U.S. to southern Mexico.
